chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that he said:

Regarding a man who prayed in the Mosque of the Tree, entered into ihram, and proclaimed the intention for Hajj, then he used perfume, hunted a bird, and had intercourse with his wife, he said: 'It is not (a major fault) until he says the Talbiyah.'

key_terms.أَهَلَّ: To proclaim the intention for Hajj
key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The ritual state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is not (a major fault/expiable act)
key_terms.يُلَبِّيَ: Recites the Talbiyah (the specific invocation for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking Ihram before reciting the Talbiyah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment the Talbiyah serves as the definitive threshold for Ihram violations, distinguishing between preparatory acts and those requiring expiation. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the verbal declaration of intention as the critical juncture for legal accountability in Hajj rituals. This ruling provides practical clarity for pilgrims regarding the permissibility of minor actions before the formal commencement of the pilgrimage rites.
